Recovered information on the zombified, Report 39B rev. 2 (Part 1 of 3)

Typewritten pages bearing stamps and emblems of the Ecological Research Group. Marked strictly confidential and signed: %c[pda_white]Arkady Tsvetkovsky%c[ui_gray_1]
Junior researcher at the RX12 laboratory and research bunker
 
Information on the walking dead, report 39B rev. 2.
 
• Date: %c[pda_white]19.03.2014%c[ui_gray_1]
• Folder: %c[pda_white]34%c[ui_gray_1]
• Page: %c[pda_white]1%c[ui_gray_1] of %c[pda_white]3%c[ui_gray_1]

“Zombified” is the term locals use for specimens of semi-living beings that can hardly be called intelligent.
Scientific data show that their brains perform no thought processes and have almost no neurological activity, confirming that brain cells have died to a critical level. Yet field tests prove that, for reasons unknown to science, their dead brains can still send impulses that trigger simple mechanical reactions, somewhat like instincts but with markedly different behavioral logic.

One theory is that endless neurochemical reactions in the body make it move in specific ways in response to particular stimuli. When threatened, they become extremely aggressive, so approach with great caution.

Tests show their physiology has changed so much that the tissues can maintain neural connections on their own. Even body parts separated from the whole can function without nutrients to produce energy. In one of the most successful experiments, the liver and heart remained functional for three months, detached from the body and disconnected from other organs and circulation.
Further analyses may reveal their molecular and subatomic peculiarities.
Recovered information on the zombified, Report 39B rev. 2 (Part 2 of 3)

Typewritten pages bearing stamps and emblems of the Ecological Research Group. Marked strictly confidential and signed: %c[pda_white]Arkady Tsvetkovsky%c[ui_gray_1]

• Page: %c[pda_white]2%c[ui_gray_1] of %c[pda_white]3%c[ui_gray_1]

Our findings may explain the mystery of how they can function indefinitely without serious difficulty after repeated wounds to their limbs, pelvic area, peripheral organs, and other regions.
Their movement is usually impaired and carrying out actions is out of the question, but their reflexes for handling weapons and pulling the trigger remain unchanged. This may also apply to the use of other simple tools and technological devices.
When dealing with deactivated specimens, do not use the terms “kill” or “destroy.” This is mostly a psychological measure: “deactivation” is more neutral than “destruction” and can reduce mental strain and suppress feelings of remorse.

Deactivating a specimen requires severing the brain’s connections to the musculoskeletal system, preferably by inflicting ballistic trauma to the brain or spinal cord. Every member of the research team must remember that the limbs remain functional even after deactivation, so extra safety measures are necessary.

More effective methods include surgically removing vertebrae or the brain stem.

In extremely rare cases, some zombified specimens behave more like intelligent animals.
They may drop their weapons or refuse to act aggressively. These specimens are of the greatest research value, so deactivating them is undesirable.
Capturing specimens and further laboratory analysis are top priorities. Neuropsychologists are especially interested in this research because of the potential to study the brain stem and transplant it. In theory, this could help patients in the late stages of Alzheimer’s and other serious diseases.

When deactivating a specimen, avoid damaging the kidneys and heart if possible. These organs have great potential for transplantation research in other viable organisms. Organs can also be collected from killed zombies, but use caution: local stalkers may have emotional ties to particular specimens.

If an encounter with stalkers is unavoidable, there are two ways to prevent a firefight.
First, when working with a rookie stalker, do not gouge out the specimen’s eyes; that is simply inhumane.
Second, when working with a veteran stalker, it is better to offer some incentive, as veterans suppress their emotions more effectively. Working with the local human population may also yield useful conclusions from psychological assessments.
Interrogation methods: fundamentals (Part 1 of 2)

Training leaflets with a large Freedom emblem in the upper-right corner and a small drawing of a pistol and a person kneeling. Titled Interrogation Methods: Fundamentals, it is written in the faction’s casual slang:

I should not even mention this, since it is obvious. Still, I will share it with you; just do not blab it everywhere or people will not understand.
Throw this leaflet away, burn it, or give it to someone you trust. You do not want everyone to learn about it, do you? You might end up in the interrogated person’s place one day. Got a stash? Keep these pages with you, and do not say later that nobody warned you.

Everyone has a hidden stash. Even the poorest, most miserable bandit in the Zone has a couple of dry rations and a few bullets tucked away. That is how things work here. You save some money, sell a few artifacts or mutant parts, rob the dead—usually still-warm—bodies, then buy food and weapons. Even when shit is flying straight into your face, you can keep grinning because you have an ace up your sleeve that might save your hide.

Those are the harsh laws of the Zone. Nobody here will help you.
Interrogation Methods: Fundamentals (Part 2 of 2)

Training leaflets with a large Freedom emblem in the upper-right corner and a small drawing of a pistol and a person kneeling. Titled Interrogation Methods: Fundamentals, it is written in the faction’s casual slang:

But now let us talk about more than help from others and stalker relations. If you want important information about someone’s stash location, start by choosing a victim.
Once you have thought it through and picked a quiet place with nobody around, shoot them in the hands and legs. Make it hurt until they realize you are their closest friend right now. Then they will drop their weapons and kneel before you.
Speak firmly and convincingly, but do not kill them. There are plenty of mutants around to finish the job for you. Let us not make the Zone worse. Tell them you will leave, scare them as much as possible, and make them understand that the end is near. They usually get the message and surrender.
Letter to Natalie
A letter written by a stalker to someone outside the Zone, probably his wife or lover. The fact that it ended up in your hands proves it will never reach its recipient.

Hello, Natalie!

How are you? How are the kids?
Tell Sasha that if he does not behave, I will give him a good spanking when I get home.

And what about me? I do not think you will understand me right now. But listen: the Zone… This place… It is unique. Only here can I feel connected to other people. Only here do I see people for who they really are.
There are no masks here, only harsh truth. I will tell you all about it in more color when we meet.
I have made good money here! We can finally buy you that necklace you have wanted for so long.
And thank you all for writing to me and not forgetting me. Your letters really help and lift my spirits even in the hardest times. When I think of you, the world becomes much simpler. See you soon. Give the kids my love!

With all my love,
— yours, Mikhail. Your brave stalker.
Stalker diary, Part 1
An old, faded notebook is wrapped in a cover to protect its pages. Time has still damaged it so badly that only part of the text can be read:

“I need to pour my soul onto paper — for some reason, I think it will make me feel better. I hope my legacy outlives me and someone finds and reads this, and I hope they do not repeat my mistakes…
I do not have many friends, and in the Zone I have none at all. The traders look at me like an outcast. That bearded guy on Zaton breaks into a sarcastic grin whenever he sees me, and Hawaiian just mocks me with his calm manner. To hell with those freaks! All I need from them is ammo and food.
 
I started this diary so someone would know what happened that night and why I prefer to be alone. I came to the Zone by myself, but quickly teamed up with this rookie… Turns out he was quite the mineral enthusiast.
He had a hobby: collecting every stone he could find. He had so many that the Zone and its artifacts seemed like the next step. He amassed such a pile that it earned him a cancerous stomach tumor. Constant vomiting, diarrhea, stress… He was like a pregnant woman, except instead of a baby he had that huge tumor. Damn. He even named it after his first puppy.
I did not mind his company. Sometimes it is better to have someone around, and the guy was decent and funny. We never bothered the bandits and tried to avoid most mutants… We just hung around anomalies and collected all sorts of strange stones along with artifacts whenever we came across them.”
Stalker diary, Part 2
An old, faded notebook is wrapped in a cover to protect its pages. Time has still damaged it so badly that only part of the text can be read:

We had all heard stories about that anomaly in a fissure deep underground. A whole mountain of artifacts was said to be down there, but for some reason nobody wanted to go.
We thought they were simply afraid. Who would fear an anomaly when there were enough artifacts to last a lifetime?!

Then we felt that rush of confidence… We gathered and headed straight for the cave. Before we could even look inside, something dark flew over us. I tripped, hit my head, and blacked out.
After a while I came to and heard groans. At first I thought they were “animals,” then realized it was my friend… lying right in front of me. His skin was torn all over, blood streamed from his muscles, and I saw bones sticking out. God, he could barely hold in his guts as he tried to crawl out of the cave. It is amazing he did not die on the spot.
I was in shock and had no idea what was happening. I do not know what came over me, but I drew my pistol and started firing into the cave darkness, acting on fear alone. I had 20 rounds and fired single shots. When I had about seven left, something jerked my hand and I fired…
I had no idea where I was shooting or where my pistol was pointed. Then the invisible force let go, but I was so full of adrenaline and fear that I kept trying to shoot for minutes after the last round was gone. I knew that if I stopped, I would see everything I had done… caused… I could not even bring myself to take his dog tags. I just ran away…

How could I talk to anyone or make another friend, knowing the Zone could simply kill them too?! No, better to be alone. Friendship costs too much. It means having friends… people who will help if something happens. It is not worth it if it cannot last, while the Zone is always ready to end a friendship and turn everything you cared about into a recurring nightmare. And this lump on my head… now it constantly reminds me what friendship costs in the Zone.
Mercenary note
A note written by a mercenary. He seems to have recorded a few thoughts about his work in the Zone. His intentions are unclear.

“
Well, all things considered, nothing I see here is particularly special. 
We’re still mercenaries, still soldiers of fortune. Even so, we can choose for ourselves what jobs to take and which ones to turn down. Sometimes we don’t accept a contract because it’s too dirty even for us. If a client wants to kill decent people who earn an honest living with their sweat and blood, forget that bastard. 
In the Zone, those problems can be handled without us. There are plenty of cutthroats already—marauders and bandits! But protecting someone is another matter. So if you need someone killed, call the scum. They’re less particular about who they murder. 
We’re different. Remember that the next time you wave your money in our faces.”
Information Report / Operation MSRC / 05.04.2014 18:36:21

Printed transcript of radio traffic between military units stationed in the Zone. The fact that this document was found among the crew of a downed SKAT indicates that they must have been involved in an underground scheme to obtain surveillance data. It states:

“- Headquarters, this is MSSRC 1-03. We’ve obtained photographs from the Research Institute, plus 240 photos of the anomalous swamp and about 1,400 of the central base. When can we return?
- MSSRC 1-03, this is Headquarters. Returning is impossible for now. There are problems at the military depots. MSRC 4-07 is requesting help. Their SOS signal is very strong at the moment; we hope they’re still alive.
- This is Headquarters. Send a helicopter.
- Negative. Anomalous activity at the Agroprom Research Institute is too high; it’s too dangerous. Proceed to Yantar. Our Mi-24 will pick you up there.
- Understood. Any information on the next blowout?
- Affirmative. Sakharov reports there are two full days until the next event. Still, hurry. His information can’t be trusted; it’s unreliable.
- Understood. We’re moving out. Tell Ptashka to be at Yantar at seven. MSSRC 1-03, out.
- Wait, 1-03. What about tunnel N-2? Did you find anything there?
- Affirmative. We found a new anomaly in it. It looks like some kind of teleporter. The eggheads at Yantar will be interested. Our electronics died when we approached it to measure the psi fields. I can’t understand where such powerful electronic waves came from.
- Copy that, MSSRC 1-03. Good luck on the way to Yantar. The helicopter will be there at seven. Headquarters, out.”
Military stalker note
A note found among someone’s belongings. It seems someone was passing the time through a long, dark night, then forgot to throw the page into the fire. The note reads:

Well… looks like I have a fresh start. I am now a military stalker, officially authorized to conduct military operations in the Zone.
All it took was a few years of clawing my way through life in this hellhole. Now all those damn soldiers who wanted to put a bullet between my eyes have to salute me. “Yes, sir!” they say. “No, sir! Three bags full!” They really follow every order. It is unreal. Special forces, riot police—everyone treats me with real respect. And yet, if I had met them last week, they would have shot me on the spot without a trial.

Now they issue me the best equipment they have, fine weapons, modern devices, and excellent food! For the first time in years, meals do not make me sick. My pay is enough to send emergency money to my wife whenever needed.

There is one catch: during missions I am forbidden to let ordinary stalkers near me or the others. The commander says I must shoot to kill if anything happens. By a cruel twist of fate, all my stalker friends are long dead, so I need not fear a fatal accident. Still, I wonder… when other stalkers see me, will I look just like the military stalkers I saw while wandering? A monster in impenetrable armor, the kind I hid from all those years…

Monolithian diary

A handwritten sheet of paper. The opening is chaotic and messy, as if the writer suffered from a severe mental disorder. Curiously, the text grows clearer and more vivid as it continues, and by the end the handwriting is nearly perfect. The note says:

As far as I can remember now, there was darkness all around me. I could not see anything. Nothing… Not even time. Then suddenly a light appeared before me! So bright, so warm… I wanted to touch it, to feel it. I understood, I knew it was trying to help me, trying to save me. I knew…

And after I touched the light, I forgot everything. There was no past life—only pitch darkness behind me. The only source of light was ahead.
Its name was the Monolith. It saved me, and I am endlessly grateful.
Sometimes faces from the past appear before me… A woman and a child… My family? I am wearing a white suit… Maybe I was a scientist… What a strange word… Radar… NO! Darkness?! It wants me dead! I WILL NOT LET IT KILL ME!
No, there is no way back! Only forward, only toward the light! Toward the light! For the Monolith!
Memoirs (Part 1 of 2)
A couple of pages torn from someone’s memoirs. The manuscript is written in blue ink, almost washed away by the elements, making it nearly illegible. The author is unknown.

I can still feel the heat of that anomaly on my back. It burns even when I am just sitting on the Skadovsk, safe from danger and away from all those heating devices. You cannot imagine what I go through every time I get near those damn anomalies.
Hell, my back burns even worse now. It has become my anomaly detector. After a fire or acid anomaly, you do not get away with ordinary burns. It is as if you have taken a piece of the Zone inside you forever. I call it Under the Zone’s Sign.

Horrifying. No law of physics works in the Zone. I simply do not know what to expect from its anomalies.
I could take on a dozen bloodsuckers in the dark, but every time I see an anomaly I just freeze… How is that possible? This cannot be real at all!
I cannot stop thinking that the whole Zone is one endless nightmare, repeating again and again.
Memoirs (Part 2 of 2)
A couple of pages torn from someone’s memoirs. The manuscript is written in blue ink, almost washed away by the elements, making it nearly illegible. The author is unknown.

Every time I think about it, my back shudders with pain and turns into one red lump.
For the last four months I have not gone anywhere near those anomalies. I make a living killing mutants, but you cannot keep that up for long.
My back still reacts as if it has a mind of its own. Sometimes I wish I had left that burning hell back then.
Maybe I would have been more useful as food for those boars. No… boars are stupid creatures. But if they attack the same Skadovsk, it will fall in a few days. Bullets will not stop them. Boars are useless animals anyway; their meat is awful, and even an experienced cook cannot make it edible.

Sometimes I wander around Zaton, though my back can barely bear the backpack. I go because I keep feeling that I left something there, something that calls to me now and then. The terrible back pain forces me to sleep on my stomach or side.
I do not like sleeping on my side; I sleep badly. The Zone changes us without asking permission.
Letter to Nikolai

A handwritten letter addressed to Nikolai. It is most likely part of a correspondence between two stalkers. Although communication in the Zone is mostly conducted by PDA, many stalkers prefer traditional letters, especially for personal matters. Couriers then carry the letters across the Zone. A letter usually reaches its recipient within a few days, and is far less likely to be intercepted than a PDA message. Couriers are highly valued among stalkers. The letter reads:

“Nikolai,

I just got back from a run to the Zone’s center. It was hell out there!

The Monolithians and the soldiers are trying to wipe each other off the map. There are lulls when it seems they’ve agreed to a ceasefire, but no such agreement exists.

It’s constant chaos and destruction. I had no choice but to get out of there. 
Those damn fanatics nearly killed me, though that was mostly my own fault—I let my guard down. Anyway, I made it to Pripyat, and I plan to stay here for a while. 
So we’ll have to postpone the mission we discussed until it’s safer here. I haven’t been sleeping much since I arrived, but I feel pretty good. Let’s keep in touch. 
Take care, Ryuk.”
Strelok has returned?

Rumor says the legendary stalker was seen again in the Zone recently. He was one of the few to reach its center.\n stalkers seem to exaggerate. %s should know more about this stalker and the situation; I should visit him.
Raid into Darkness — Information
%c[pda_white]Raid into Darkness statistics:\n
Secrets of the Zone

Strelok has an old friend hiding in the Zone. Finding him could reveal more about the Zone. If only I knew where to look...\nThe Forester, an old man in the Red Forest, must know something. These two legends may know each other.
Note from Aslan
Aslan has a rather strange hobby: he collects faction patches. He won’t say why.\nAs he put it:

“Basically, for 25 patches from any faction except scientists and fanatics—we’ll get to them later—you get a chance at some kind of artifact, or you may get nothing.
With 50, you have a chance at a better artifact and some gear used by experienced stalkers; the odds of getting nothing are lower.
But 25 Monolith or scientist patches get you a pretty decent artifact, with the same odds as 50 patches from other factions.
With 50 Monolith or scientist patches, you get an excellent artifact and decent gear for veteran stalkers. There’s no chance of getting nothing.
 
You’ll ask why I’m so generous? Many prefer to keep patches as trophies.”
Note from Gryphon

Gryphon and his crew are stuck on the outskirts of Pripyat, but they can’t leave the city empty-handed. One of the secret X-Labs is somewhere in the northern part of the city. The mercs need the documents, if any are still there.\nGryphon promised a decent reward. If I remember right, he said:

“We came here for information from Lab X-8. It lies beneath the local department store; its elevator can take you to the minus-first floor. But those damned soldiers got in our way, and now we’re in this miserable state. The way things stand, Dusman will finish us off, but there may still be some papers left there. If we knew for sure, we’d already be thinking about how to get out of here. I’d go with the guys, but there are too few of us left as it is, and we’d still have to fight our way back from the Zone’s center.\nHere’s my offer: search X-8—maybe there’s something left—and we’ll pay you a decent sum on top.”
Note from Tikhiy

Despite the situation Gryphon and his squad are in, Tikhiy has access to top-quality weapons. To buy anything from him, I first need to make a deal with him.\nHe says I can order only one item at a time, and he doesn’t take advance payment. He’ll message me when the goods arrive. Here’s his price list:

Pistols and SMGs:













 • “Steppe Eagle” — 8,000 rubles. Apparently a Desert Eagle modified with hand-fitted parts.
 • “Alpine” — 6,500 rubles. A SIG220 variant with an enlarged magazine.
 • “Marsh” — 7,000 rubles. A fast-firing, hard-hitting USP pistol variant.
 • MP-5 “Frasier” — 9,500 rubles. He swears this one is entirely handmade, with improved specs.

Shotguns:
 • “Carabiner” — 11,000 rubles. A military SPAS-12 variant with reduced recoil and automatic fire.

Rifles:
 • “Storm” — 19,000 rubles. A Groza variant from specialists; supposedly the batch “secretly” leaked to the public. Comes with an enlarged magazine.
 • H&K G36 — 14,000 rubles. Yes, this really is a rare find in the Zone.

 • SVD “Lynx” — 18,000 rubles. A military variant combining accuracy and stopping power.

Protective gear:
 • Monolith exoskeleton — 100,000 rubles. According to Tikhiy, it offers the best protection. You can’t get one anywhere else, either.
 • Mercenary exoskeleton — 75,000 rubles. Tikhiy claims this is probably the most reliable protection available.
 • Bandit exoskeleton — 65,000 rubles. A truly “serious” exclusive.
 • Monolith suit with a closed-loop breathing system — 70,000 rubles. Where does he even get these?
